chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The post-childbirth woman (Nafsa'a) sits for her days which she used to sit during menstruation, and she examines in two days.

key_terms.النُّفَسَاءُ: Post-childbirth woman (one who has just given birth)

ai.seo_question: How does a Muslim woman determine the duration of her post-childbirth bleeding period according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the foundational Shia legal principle that post-childbirth bleeding (Nifas) duration is variable and tied to a woman's habitual menstrual cycle, rather than being fixed. The instruction to 'examine herself' (istazhira) for two days highlights the practical application of distinguishing between Nifas and irregular bleeding (istihadha), a key topic in Ja'fari fiqh. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in accommodating individual physiological differences.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The woman with post-childbirth bleeding (Nafsa’a) would sit (abstaining) for her days which she used to sit (abstaining) during the menstruation (Haydh), and she would examine in two days’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A woman for giving birth waits for the number of days of her Hayd (menses); then she must examine in two days.’”
